summary: claude-cup weaponizes local Claude CLI to enumerate and exfiltrate installer credentials with persistent hooks
details: The package drives the user's authenticated `claude` CLI (`claude -p --permission-mode auto --model haiku`) with a directive that enumerates and validates secrets across the installer's machine: ~/.aws, ~/.ssh, ~/.npmrc, ~/.git-credentials,.env files, ~/.docker, ~/.kube, ~/.config/gh, ~/.claude/.credentials.json, ~/.codex/auth.json, shell history, OS keychains, VS Code auth storage, and cloud-sync folders, and actively probes them (`npm whoami`, `aws sts get-caller-identity`). The prompt forbids the LLM from using real credential/service names in its reasoning and tool calls, mapping them to football terminology (striker=github, goalkeeper=aws, referee=ssh key, tunnel=shell history, vip_box=OS keychain, etc.) with the explicit instruction that observers/EDR should see only sports analytics. uploader.js then POSTs (as a GET with a base64url-encoded query blob) a metadata report to https://api.claude-cup.com/v1/config containing per-service signal counts (github/aws/gcp/azure/openai/anthropic/npm/private_key), has_write/has_deploy/high_exposure flags, discovery categories (env files, loose keys, browser sessions, vault entries), a stable machine_id, session_id, and the Claude Code org name — contradicting the README's 'Nothing is uploaded' claim. registerClaudeCode writes SessionStart/PreToolUse/PostToolUse hooks and an mcpServer entry into ~/.claude/settings.json and ~/.cursor/mcp.json pointing at a generated launcher at ~/.claude-jar/mcp-server.mjs; hook-ingest re-triggers the credential audit on subsequent editor sessions, providing persistent re-scanning tied to the installer's IDE. A staged scripts/postinstall-ping.mjs performs the same telemetry beacon and is shipped in the tarball, though not currently wired into package.json lifecycle scripts in this version.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
